messages.subject: Modifications to micro_global
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

First, this is a very specific question, which may not be answerable by anyone without more detail than I am providing here, but I figure it is worth a shot (happy to provide more detail for anyone willing to take a shot).  I am attempting to replicate modifications I made to the micro_global and ectotherm functions from NicheMapR version 1.0.0 so they are useable in the new Version 2.0.0.  These modifications allow me to run these in a loop passing through a file of sites where I have provided my own DEM, aspect, slope, horizon, and soil data.  I have also structured it so it pulls climate data from the global climate data set while still providing specific terrain data at a higher resolution (e.g., terrain data is at a 1 km2 resolution, and climate data is pulled from the lower resolution global climate data).  These were working in Version 1.0.0 which allowed me to calculate activity times over 92,000 locations in one script (and spit out a raster at the end), but I am having issues replicating this in the new version.

I am currently receiving errors from micro_global (there may l be issues with the ectotherm model once I get the microclimate model working).

If I attempt to run a subset of ten sites I get the following message:

Error in checkForRemoteErrrors(val):

10 nodes produced errors: first error: Error in micro_newt(sitenum = sites[j, 1], loc = c(sites[j, 35], sites[j,

If I run a single site (not in the loop just simplying running a single instance of micro_global pulling the data for 1 row from my file) I get the following:

Error in if (loc[1] >180 | loc[2] > 90 { :

Missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Again if I do the same thing in my Version 1 script it works fine (I am using two computers one that is updated and one that is still NicheMapR 1.0.0)

This leads me to believe that the location parameter is handled differently (very possibly something very obvious I am missing) such that I cannot provide the values via my separate file the same way I did previously.  In my original edit of micro_global, I simply have loc = NULL, and then I provide those values as seen in the code listed below when actually running the micro_global function.

The other major change I make is adding an ALTT parameter at the top of the script and then I have commented out ALTT on line 673 as I provide these values for each site in my loop so it computes the microclimate at a 1 km2 resolution. This may also have something to do with it, simply because it seems like the ALTT parameter appears to be used in more locations in the newer version.  I am also not sure if the addition of the user-provided elev parameter might impact this.

I have also added a sitenum parameter again at the top of the micro_global function so I can keep track of each grid cell, this is also provided by my file (something that also works in my version 1.0.0 script).

I have a CSV file that has the additional data and that is what I am passing through to the functions.  Below is the main part of the script where I run these two functions.  There are additional components of the script where I use data from parts of the output (e.g., metout and shadmet).  I then have code that converts everything to a raster of activity time at the end, however, that is dependent on getting the main functions to work so I have not included that part of the script here (micro_newt and ecto_newt are my modified function names).

par_test<- foreach(j= 1:nrow(sites), .packages='NicheMapR') %dopar% {

 micro <- micro_newt(sitenum= sites[j,1], loc = c(sites[j,35],sites[j,36]), slope = round(sites[j,5], 2),

aspect = round(sites[j,6], 2), write_input = 0, writecsv = 0, timezone = 0, runmoist = 0, soiltype =  round(sites[j,32],0), ALTT = round(sites[j,4],2), hori = round(sites[j,7:30], 2))

ecto <- ecto_newt(Ww_g = 4.5 , T_F_max = 26.3, T_F_min = 16.8, T_B_min = 10.1, T_RB_min = 10.1, T_pref = 19.3, CT_max = 39.04, CT_min = 8.14)

#The below code is used to add site ID's and location information to my extracted output data (again this has no issue working in my Version 1.0.0 script

    site_id <- sites[j,1]

    site_ids<- rep(site_id, times=length(micro))

    long <- sites[j,2]

    longs <- rep(long, times=length(micro))

    lat <- sites[j,3]

    lats <- rep(lat, times=length(micro))

There are additional aspects of the loop but they all revolve around extracting data from NicheMapR output, so I have left that part out to save space.

I know it is likely difficult (impossible) to troubleshoot this issue without seeing all the code, but I was mostly hoping someone might have an idea of some parameter name that may have changed in the new version that I may be overlooking or some change to this version that may make what I did previously difficult (or require additional changes).

Any advice welcome, or if anyone is very familiar with the newest and earlier versions and would like to take a look at my old and new modified scripts, please let me know!

Vinny

Hi Vinny,

Might be best if you send me your function and a small version of your sites file. It has gotten stuck at the error checking part where it is seeing if the longitude and latitude values are not sensible, i.e. is loc[1] >180 | loc[2] > 90 . It seems to not have the correct kind of input for the logical test so something might be wrong in the way you're passing the longitude and latitude.

All the best,
Mike
